propositions: Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.8 both declare a 1,000,000-token context window, so escalation from sonnet to opus gains zero additional capacity and guarantees a second failure at higher cost.

A sonnet-primary context-limit retry loop silently consumes two attempts (one at sonnet pricing, one at opus pricing) but never actually escalates, making the diagnosis appear more alarming than reality (misleading operator inference that even opus failed, rather than that escalation was ineffective).
Both declared window figures are verified correct against the provider's live Models API, so the defect is in escalation consumption logic, not in the declared values themselves.

The new escalation_rungs() function filters models_at_or_above() to exclude rungs whose declared window is not strictly greater than the last kept rung, skipping the no-op opus escalation while preserving the unchanged models_at_or_above() contract and task 7761's provider-stickiness tests.
Haiku-to-sonnet escalation (a genuine 800k-token increase) and all non-escalation consumers (largest_window_tokens, model-class vocabulary) remain unchanged and unaffected.
